device_authorization.scope: Documentation supplement only; it is not an OpenAPI operation and is not included in operation_count_observed.
facts: The guide describes RFC 8628 device authorization for CLI and external-app browser sign-in.
It documents POST /api/auth/device/code, browser approval, then POST /api/auth/device/token; the issued token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
It states that self-hosted Kaneo allows the built-in device client IDs kaneo-cli and kaneo-mcp by default, and other IDs require DEVICE_AUTH_CLIENT_IDS approval.
gaps: The vendored OpenAPI snapshot contains GET /auth/device but does not contain the documented POST /auth/device/code or POST /auth/device/token endpoints, so neither is mapped as an OpenAPI operation.

The authentication guide gives examples and polling error names but does not establish this CLI's final client ID, storage policy, browser-launch behavior, or complete machine-readable request and response schemas.

The guide says all API endpoints require authentication, while individual OpenAPI operations can override inherited security; future implementation must follow the endpoint-level OpenAPI security declaration and verify live behavior.

task_reserved_statuses.relationship: The pinned OpenAPI describes a task status only as an unconstrained string and describes PUT /task/status/{id} as a move to another column. Upstream declares two additional reserved values at the revision the previous snapshot was taken from; the declaring file is byte-identical at d4dc32bebd3b8f16e314d6bc875c3e6502abb883 (v2.27.0), and at 100027a7f9ccce4f5d650f0e45770b9f36dfad2e (v2.28.3), the current snapshot revision, it still declares VIRTUAL_STATUSES as ["planned", "archived"]; that release only adds multiselect custom-field validation to the file. This supplement is help text only; it is evidence for the contract, not a modification of the pinned snapshot.
task_reserved_statuses.scope: CLI help supplement only. The pinned OpenAPI, the generated operation inventory and the generated request-body reference remain unchanged.
task_reserved_statuses.evidence: Disposable pinned Kaneo (image digest recorded in docs/verification.md): writing status "planned" or "archived" through updateTaskStatus returned HTTP 200 with columnId null and moved the task into the board's plannedTasks or archivedTasks container; writing a column slug back restored it with a non-null columnId. createTask accepted "planned" directly. moveTask rejected destinationStatus "planned" with HTTP 400 "Selected status is not valid for the destination project". An unknown status on updateTaskStatus returned HTTP 400 and left the task unchanged. importTasks accepted an unknown status, stored it as "planned" and reported success with a per-task warning. listTasks --status planned returned only the planned container. See docs/verification.md.
task_reserved_statuses.constraints: Valid task statuses are the project's column slugs plus the reserved values "planned" and "archived" (upstream VIRTUAL_STATUSES). A column may not be created with either reserved slug, so the board's three containers cannot collide. moveTask accepts destination column slugs only.
